proposal.name: Let Python commands open private Docker mounts

plan.name: Let Python commands open private Docker mounts
plan.summary: Run existing Python application commands with an explicit Docker --user: the gate's effective host UID:GID for ordinary Docker, or 0:0 for rootless Docker, whose container root maps to the host daemon owner; identify the selected daemon using docker info --format '{{json .SecurityOptions}}' before launching the command. Refuse failed or malformed identity discovery and rootful user-namespace remapping with a diagnostic before launching, without fallback, and preserve private directory and authentication-file permissions, offline networking, the read-only root and input mounts, writable output, dropped capabilities, no new privileges, resource limits, tmpfs restrictions, interpreter and environment settings, image selection, overlays and cancellation cleanup. Add TestPythonApplicationGatePrivateMounts in an integration-tagged file, running the existing standard-library application fixture with explicit components through real Docker Python and TLC without an environment opt-in: an honest application must pass, while an invalid transition must produce a real TLC BadStep after successful Python test and driver executions, so the existing Linux integration shards exercise mount access automatically. Adapt the four named existing Docker doubles only to answer the new formatted security-options query while retaining their existing assertions and unformatted-info refusal behavior, and update SPEC.md and README.md to describe the identity policy, supported rootless mapping, refusal of rootful remapping and automatic integration coverage, retaining the relevant decision citations including D-0181, D-0183, D-0185, D-0197 and D-0122. Merger work is to record the new execution-identity decision refining D-0181 and add its SPEC citation, confirm the real integration gate passes on Linux and the existing real Python execution and gate suites still pass on macOS, with unavailable Docker or network checks reported as merger work.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationDockerUsesMountOwner
tests.says: Ordinary Docker runs application commands as the effective host UID and GID, preserving private mount permissions, all existing isolation limits, read-only overlays, arguments and application output.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationDockerUsesRootlessRoot
tests.says: Rootless Docker runs application commands as container 0:0, which maps to the host daemon owner, with the same private mounts and all existing isolation limits.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationDockerRefusesUnknownIdentity
tests.says: Failed or malformed daemon identity discovery and unsupported rootful user-namespace remapping stop before any application container launches, leaving private permissions intact.

usage.summary: Created `plan.json` and acceptance tests covering Docker identity selection, preserved isolation, Linux integration coverage, and documentation updates. All three tests compile and fail on the baseline as required, but the checker timed out twice, leaving full plan validation unconfirmed.
